subject: Follow-up: multilingual evals & model recommendations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Berger <anna.berger@euroretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-25T14:12:00-05:00
Subject: Follow-up: multilingual evals & model recommendations

Hi Anna —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size the evaluation properly: 

Recap from the call
- Goal: evaluate model fit for product descriptions + localized customer Q&A across EU languages (FR, DE, ES, NL) and APAC (JA, KO, ZH-Hans).
- Primary concerns: translation/localization fidelity, factual consistency for catalog attributes, and latency targets for the on-site search flow (~150-250ms p50).
- Data: you mentioned a 5k sample per locale we can use for evaluation (sanitized).

Recommended initial model candidates (based on similar retail workloads):
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (cost-efficient, often strong on EU languages)
- Llama-2-70B-chat (higher-quality baseline, good for long-context generation)
- Falcon-180B-Instruct (strong few-shot performance but heavier latency/cost)
- Our Redwood-multilang-13B-quant (Redwood-verified quantized variant; lower cost, may have regressions in certain APAC locales)

What we’ll deliver
1) A small evaluation run across the 5k/sample prompt set per locale covering: translation accuracy (BLEU/chrF), answer correctness (human-eval tags), hallucination rate, latency & cost estimates.
2) A short deck with model recommendations per locale and a prompt-set CSV (attached: prompt_set_v1.csv).
3) A follow-up call to review results and recommend an MLP (model + quantization + routing) configuration for production.

Next steps (proposed timeline)
- You confirm the final list of locales and share sanitized samples (we can accept S3/Drive links or a signed upload URL) — due by 2026-02-27.
- Redwood runs evals and shares preliminary benchmark spreadsheet by 2026-03-02.
- Review call the week of 2026-03-08.

Please confirm the locales and whether the 5k/sample is feasible. Also confirm any compliance or data residency constraints we should account for in the evaluation (EU GDPR specifics, data retention windows, etc.).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193

Attachment: prompt_set_v1.csv (CSV stub, 3 columns: locale, prompt_template, validation_id)

From: Anna Berger <anna.berger@euroretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-26T09:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: multilingual evals & model recommendations

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming locales: FR, DE, ES, NL, JA, KO, ZH-Hans. 5k per locale is fine but we need the evaluation process to avoid storing any PII; everything must be sanitized as discussed.

Notes/constraints:
- EU data must remain within EU regions where possible for pre-production artifacts; can you run the initial evals on EU-resident infra?
- Latency target: p50 <= 250ms for short generation (product attribute answers). p95 can be higher but please surface both.
- Budget sensitivity: we’d prefer to start with smaller (7B-13B) candidates for cost reasons and then compare to the 70B baseline if the quality delta warrants it.

We can share sanitized samples via an S3 bucket. I’ll invite our security contact if you need formal ATO / DTO info.

Best,
Anna
Anna Berger
Head of ML Integrations | EuroRetail Ltd
anna.berger@euroretail.com

--- On privacy: please send any links to evaluation outputs to our EU-owned Drive only.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-27T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: multilingual evals & model recommendations — action: run evals

Team —

Please take ownership of the EuroRetail evals. Requirements:
- Locales: FR, DE, ES, NL, JA, KO, ZH-Hans (5k samples each). Samples will be provided in sanitized S3.
- Metrics: BLEU/chrF, exact-match on structured attribute extraction, hallucination rate (human-tagged), latency p50/p95, token cost estimate.
- Run models/configs: Mistral-7B-Instruct, Redwood-multilang-13B (fp16 + int8 quant), Llama-2-70B-chat (baseline), Falcon-180B-Instruct (optional, if cost allows).
- Run quantized variants for cost comparison but note any quality regressions by locale.
- Host initial runs in EU region for compliance; if infra not available, flag immediately.

Deliverables by 2026-03-02: a spreadsheet (per-locale tabs) with metrics and a short notes section for any observed regressions. Attach the benchmark file to the thread and provide a Drive link.

Ping me if infra or data access is blocked.

—Marissa

Attachment: redwood_eval_run_instructions.md (stub)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: multilingual evals & model recommendations — action: run evals

Marissa —

Quick update and preliminary findings from the run we started yesterday (note: we replicated using EU-hosted infra). Full spreadsheet attached (redwood_multilang_benchmarks_q1_2026.xlsx). Highlights:

- Data: received sanitized S3; scripts validated locales and headers.
- Throughput/latency (p50) on baseline instances: Mistral-7B: ~95ms (FR/DE), Redwood-13B-fp16: ~120ms, Redwood-13B-int8: ~95ms, Llama-2-70B-chat: ~310ms (higher), Falcon-180B: ~420ms.
- Quality (summary):
  - FR/DE/ES/NL: Mistral-7B and Redwood-13B-fp16 are comparable on BLEU/chrF; int8 quant shows ~2-3 point drop in chrF on DE and NL.
  - JA/KO/ZH-Hans: Llama-2-70B-chat remains best overall but the quality gap vs Redwood-13B is smaller than expected on KO; however the int8 quant for Redwood-13B shows a bigger regression on JA/KO (human eval shows higher hallucination rates ~5% delta).
- Cost roughing: int8 variants reduce token cost ~35% vs fp16 for Redwood-13B.

Notes / action items:
- For APAC (JA/KO) I recommend running a targeted human-eval with native speakers on the top 500 prompts before we recommend int8 in production; regressions are non-trivial for some prompt templates.
- Rishi is testing an alternative quant profile that may reduce the JA/KO regressions; ETA 48 hours.

Links: Drive (EU): https://drive.google.com/redwood/evals/rdw-2389

I’ll update the spreadsheet with per-locale example failures and the exact cost math.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_multilang_benchmarks_q1_2026.xlsx (spreadsheet stub, per-locale tabs with metrics)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Berger <anna.berger@euroretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: multilingual evals & model recommendations

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing the samples. We’ve completed the initial pass and attached the benchmark spreadsheet (redwood_multilang_benchmarks_q1_2026.xlsx). Short summary:

- Recommendation (MVP): Redwood-multilang-13B-fp16 for EU locales (FR/DE/ES/NL) — best balance of latency and quality.
- APAC recommendation: run a controlled pilot using Llama-2-70B-chat for JA/KO for the highest quality, and Redwood-13B-int8 only after the smaller human-eval validation (Dev flagged ~5% hallucination uptick on some JA/KO templates).
- If budget is strict, Mistral-7B-Instruct is a strong cost-effective candidate for EU locales but we saw slightly worse structured-extraction scores on nested attributes.

Proposed next steps:
1) Sign off on the MVP per-locale configuration (I recommend signing off on Redwood-13B-fp16 for EU and a pilot on Llama-2-70B for APAC).
2) We’ll run the 500-sample native-speaker human-eval for JA/KO (estimated 3 business days) to validate the int8 path.
3) Post-pilot, we’ll share an SOW addendum with target SLA/latency tiers and an estimated monthly cost bucket for the chosen config.

I’ll set up a review call for 2026-03-09 to go over examples and the decision matrix unless you’d prefer earlier.

Let me know if EU Drive link is the right place to put the full spreadsheet (we used EU Drive per your note).

Best —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
